explanation: The physical element that Jesus uses to illustrate the eternal joy of life he gives, in contrast to the ordinary water from Jacob's well.
This region between Galilee and Judea where the Samaritans lived; Jews usually avoided this place due to religious and ethnic tensions.
A woman whom Jesus meets at the well, whose life story with five husbands is revealed to show his insight into human needs.
In this context, it concerns how one honors God; Jesus proclaims that true worship happens "in Spirit and truth" independent of geographic location such as Mount Gerizim or Jerusalem.
The Greek term for 'Messiah' (anointed), the title of the Savior whom the Samaritan believes is coming, which Jesus confirms he is.
A metaphorical expression for eternal life and spiritual satisfaction that only Christ can give, in contrast to temporarily quenching thirst.
